Closest lexical precedent: [Marwah & Beel (2020)](https://aclanthology.org/2020.wosp-1.5/) compare time-normalized TF-IDF against ordinary TF-IDF, reporting improvements across three retrieval datasets; this supports recency-sensitive lexical weighting, but does not establish sequential-recommendation gains. [Pazzani & Billsus (2007)](https://cs.fit.edu/~pkc/apweb/related/pazzani07aw.pdf) describe established TF-IDF content profiles. I found no study directly comparing recent-title/description pooling, recency weighting, distinct-item lexical agreement, and support shrinkage as residuals over SASRec under the stated restrictions. Novelty therefore remains plausible for the particular mechanism and controlled evaluation, rather than TF-IDF profiling itself.

Adjacent sequential evidence has different assumptions. [TASTE (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2308.14029) reports reduced popularity bias and compares text-only versus identifier-plus-text modeling; its qualitative example contrasts same-brand recommendations with more relevant product-type matches. It uses pretrained T5, and this example is not a controlled brand-removal ablation. [UniT (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13530) documents excessive clustering of semantically similar item representations, motivating caution about repeated similarity. [Basaran et al. (2017)](https://aiml-research.github.io/files/17.SDM.pdf) demonstrate that Amazon product-variant redundancies can distort evaluation and algorithm rankings; their rating-prediction setting does not quantify this benchmark’s exposure. These findings do not establish robustness to boilerplate or near-duplicate titles.

Needed ablations, proposed rather than established: hold the SASRec checkpoint and candidate sets fixed; compare last-item TF-IDF, uniform recent-window pooling, recency-weighted pooling, distinct-item support, then support shrinkage such as n/(n+λ). Count each term once per distinct item. Repeat scoring with title-inferred brand tokens masked, recurring description templates removed, and near-duplicate history items contributing at most one support vote. Preserve benchmark splits; report paired validation HR@10 changes and diagnostic slices. Gains surviving these controls would strengthen evidence for relevance beyond metadata shortcuts.
